Definition: from Ἄτταλος (a king of Pergamus); Attaleia, a place in Pamphylia:--Attalia.
BiblicalUsage: Attalia was the port in Pamphylia where Paul and Barnabas stopped on their way back to Antioch after preaching in Perga. It appears only here, at the end of the first missionary journey.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the port matters because it marks the road home, and the journey that began with a sending ended with a return and a report.
